Our Story

Peace is built through journalism

The Peace Journalism Foundation East Africa works at the intersection of conflict, media, and community resilience. Since 2014, we have trained journalists, strengthened editorial standards, and built the infrastructure for responsible reporting across the region.

Our work is grounded in evidence, shaped by local communities, and recognised by international development partners. We train journalists not just to survive conflict, but to actively help resolve it — through accurate, empathetic, solutions-oriented storytelling.

Our Approach

Four pillars of lasting change

I
The Human Lens

Centering individual stories to illuminate systemic realities. We train journalists to report on people, not just events — rebuilding trust between media and communities.

II
Structural Change

Reforming editorial cultures and newsroom policies so that peace-oriented journalism becomes the professional standard, not the exception across East Africa.

III
Solutions Journalism

Moving beyond the problem to report on responses, evidence, and innovation. Equipping journalists with frameworks to cover what works, not only what fails.

IV
Cultural Transformation

Building a generation of peace ambassadors through youth poetry clubs, community dialogues, and media literacy programmes that reshape how citizens engage with information.

Our Journey

A decade of impact

2014
Foundation established in Kampala
PJF East Africa launches with a mandate to professionalise conflict reporting across Uganda and the wider East Africa region.
2016
First training cohort — 45 journalists trained
Inaugural conflict-sensitive journalism training delivered in partnership with DW Akademie. Participants from Uganda, South Sudan, and DRC.
2018
Peace Journalism Awards launched
First annual awards ceremony held in Kampala, recognising excellence in peace-oriented journalism across East Africa.
2020
Youth Poetry Peace Clubs launched
Community engagement programme launched in 20 schools across northern Uganda, integrating peace messaging into creative arts education.
2022
Expansion to 7 countries · GIZ-CPS partnership
Programmes extend to Kenya, Rwanda, Burundi, and Sudan. Partnership with GIZ-CPS established for a regional media capacity initiative.
2026
800+ journalists trained milestone
PJF East Africa marks over a decade having trained 800+ journalists, published research reports, and engaged 60+ media houses across 7 countries.

Support Our Work

Fund the journalism that builds peace

Every contribution directly funds training, fellowships, research, and community programmes across East Africa.

🕊️
Poetry Peace Clubs Fund
Inspiring the next generation

Youth poetry clubs in schools across northern Uganda use creative arts to explore peace, conflict, and identity. Your support trains facilitators and reaches 2,000+ young people each year.

🏆
Peace Journalism Awards Fund
Celebrating excellence

The annual awards recognise journalists producing work that advances peace. Your support funds prizes, the gala, and a visibility campaign that amplifies award-winning stories across the region.

📱
Digital Peace Influencers Fund
Peace in the digital age

Training young digital content creators to produce peace-oriented social media content, combating misinformation where it spreads most — online. 50 influencers trained per cohort.

✍️
Journalist Fellowship Fund
Building future leaders

A six-month immersive fellowship placing emerging journalists with mentors, newsrooms, and field assignments. Your contribution directly sponsors one fellow through their entire journey.
